statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-50149 (GHSA-g3xr-5w5j-w4q4, GO-2026-5889): in Contour, the Kubernetes ingress controller for Envoy, an HTTPProxy that combines spec.virtualhost.tls.enableFallbackCertificate: true with spec.virtualhost.jwtProviders was accepted, so requests from clients that send no TLS SNI, or an SNI that matches no HTTPProxy, bypassed JWT verification and reached the upstream services without a valid token. It is fixed in Contour 1.33.5, which rejects that combination: https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/security/advisories/GHSA-g3xr-5w5j-w4q4, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5889, https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/releases/tag/v1.33.5 . The Go vulnerability database lists no vulnerable functions for this entry. The fix is commit https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/commit/4cb1dcb459fb30f8839fe534ab594cbc58eabf50 on release-1.33, which adds the check to HTTPProxyProcessor.computeHTTPProxy in internal/dag/httpproxy_processor.go; its other changes are a test and documentation. Between v1.33.4 and v1.33.5, the other changes outside tests, documentation, examples and CI workflows are the Go and dependency versions in go.mod, go.sum and the Makefile, and the default image tag in cmd/contour/gatewayprovisioner.go; nothing under apis/ changed. We downloaded every external-dns-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions from 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each published for both architectures, and checked each download against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, plus directories; no package contains a symbolic link. We read the function table (pclntab) and build information of the program in every build and searched its bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions; runtime.main is in the function table of every build. The Go release by build: 0.20.0-r0 Go 1.25.7; 0.20.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r0 Go 1.26.1; 0.21.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r2 Go 1.26.2; 0.21.0-r3 to 0.21.0-r5 Go 1.26.3; 0.21.0-r6 to 0.21.0-r7 Go 1.26.4; 0.21.0-r8 to 0.21.0-r11 Go 1.26.5; 0.21.0-r12 Go 1.26.6; 0.21.0-r13 to 0.22.0-r0 Go 1.26.7; 0.22.0-r1 to 0.22.0-r3 Go 1.26.8; 0.23.0-r1 to 0.23.0-r2 Go 1.27.1; 0.23.0-r3 Go 1.27.2; 0.23.0-r4 to 0.24.0-r2 Go 1.27.3; 0.24.0-r3 to 0.24.0-r5 Go 1.27.4. The build information lists github.com/projectcontour/contour v1.33.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r4, v1.33.3 in 0.21.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r3, v1.33.4 in 0.21.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r8, v1.33.5 in 0.21.0-r9 to 0.21.0-r13, v1.33.6 in 0.22.0-r0 to 0.22.0-r3 and v1.33.7 in 0.23.0-r1 to 0.24.0-r5. In every build, every Contour function in the function table is in package github.com/projectcontour/contour/apis/projectcontour/v1, the HTTPProxy API types; no function from any github.com/projectcontour/contour/internal/ package is present. The byte search of every build finds neither github.com/projectcontour/contour/internal/ nor computeHTTPProxy, while github.com/projectcontour/contour/apis/ names are present in every build. As a positive control, the same function-table reader run on Contour's own contour program, built from v1.33.3 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, finds internal/dag.(*HTTPProxyProcessor).computeHTTPProxy in its function table. The builds that list Contour 1.33.0, 1.33.3 or 1.33.4 are inside the advisory's version range, but the vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.
